claims.claim_text: The sustainability-related financial disclosures are prepared for the same reporting entity as the related general purpose financial statements.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Key preparation principles > Reporting entity and boundary
claims.support_notes: Explicitly states same reporting entity.

claims.claim_text: The sustainability-related financial disclosures cover the same reporting period as the related financial statements and are reported at the same time.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Key preparation principles > Reporting period and timing
claims.support_notes: States same period and same time; also implies linkage to related financial statements.

claims.claim_text: Amounts presented in currency are reported in euros (EUR), the same presentation currency as the related financial statements.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.1 Basis of preparation, reporting period, currency and comparatives
draft_markdown: Key preparation principles > Presentation currency
claims.support_notes: Direct statement of EUR and alignment with financial statements.

claims.claim_text: The reporting year is 2024 with a fiscal year end of 31 December 2024.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.1 Basis of preparation, reporting period, currency and comparatives
claims.support_notes: Identifies period and year-end; ties to related financial statements later in section.

claims.claim_text: Where comparative information is presented, the comparative years are 2022 and 2023.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.1 Basis of preparation, reporting period, currency and comparatives
claims.support_notes: Comparability principle supported by explicit comparative years.

claims.claim_text: Climate-related capital expenditure (climate capex) is EUR 322.2 million (2022), EUR 373.91 million (2023) and EUR 476.95 million (2024).
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.1 Selected multi-year measures > Climate-related capital expenditure (climate capex)
claims.support_notes: Multi-year metric presented to support comparability.

claims.claim_text: Tier 1 capital is EUR 95,149.4 million (2022), EUR 143,979.2 million (2023) and EUR 151,208.6 million (2024).
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.1 Selected multi-year measures > Tier 1 capital
claims.support_notes: Presented as connected to general purpose financial reporting; Tier 1 capital cited as also in financial statements.

claims.claim_text: For 2024, financed emissions are 35,973,167.6878965 tCO2e and carbon intensity is 1,154.8131 tCO2e per EUR million.
claims.support_notes: Metrics disclosed with units; referenced as portfolio-level metrics supporting understanding and connectivity.

claims.claim_text: The disclosures should be read together with the related financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024, because some measures (for example, Tier 1 capital) are also presented in general purpose financial reporting.
claims.support_notes: Explicit cross-reference and rationale for connectivity.

claims.claim_text: The objective of the disclosures is to present material sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect the entity’s prospects, including effects on cash flows, access to finance and cost of capital over the short, medium and long term.
claims.support_notes: Mirrors IFRS S1 objective/prospects framing and materiality requirement.

claims.claim_text: The climate-related risk register identifies a risk titled "Physical risk — mortgage book flood exposure", categorised as acute physical risk and rated critical.
entities: Physical risk — mortgage book flood exposure
claims.support_notes: Specific risk, category and rating are stated; supports fair presentation and risk management core content.

claims.claim_text: For the mortgage flood exposure risk, residential and commercial mortgage collateral in flood-prone zones faces rising acute physical risk, and property damage and devaluation could impair collateral coverage, affecting loss given default and credit outcomes.
claims.support_notes: Describes mechanism linking sustainability risk to financial effects (credit metrics), supporting additional information about effects.

claims.claim_text: Examples of transition and stakeholder-related risks include rapid electrification, minimum energy performance standards affecting EPC collateral, stakeholder/NGO scrutiny of financed emissions and fossil financing, and chronic heat/shifting precipitation affecting agricultural counterparties.
claims.support_notes: Provides examples across strategy/risk management; qualitative only.

claims.claim_text: In 2024, green loans are 10.71% as an indicator of portfolio positioning.
claims.support_notes: Metric disclosed and linked to understanding exposure/positioning.

claims.claim_text: Governance disclosures state the board size is 10; board climate expertise is 33.5%; climate topics appear on the board agenda 69.8% of the time; the board meets 4 times per year; and climate risk reporting is provided semi-annually.
claims.support_notes: Quantified governance oversight indicators provided.

claims.claim_text: An ESG committee is in place and meets 5 times per year; management-level governance structures include the Group Sustainability Committee, the ESG Executive Committee, and the Climate Risk Management Committee.
claims.support_notes: Lists committees and meeting frequency for ESG committee.

claims.claim_text: The climate risk register includes defined monitoring frequencies and a "changed since prior period" indicator; monitoring frequencies include monthly, quarterly and semi-annual, and the mortgage flood exposure risk is monitored monthly.
claims.support_notes: Describes monitoring design and example frequency.

claims.claim_text: The risk rating approach uses a 5x5 risk matrix based on likelihood score multiplied by severity score; for the mortgage flood exposure risk, likelihood is 4 and severity is 5, giving a score of 20 and a critical rating.
claims.support_notes: Provides defined calculation and a worked example.

claims.claim_text: The entity applies NGFS v4 Net Zero 2050 using a top-down sector-pathway approach to the banking book; carbon price assumptions from the IEA NZE 2050 trajectory are mapped to counterparty NACE sectors; stranded asset estimates are derived from sector-level fossil fuel capex exposure; scope covers lending exposures across DE, FR, IT, NL and ES.
claims.support_notes: Method and scope described; no quantitative outputs provided here.

claims.claim_text: Under orderly transition scenarios, the portfolio demonstrates adequate resilience with transition risk losses remaining within Pillar 2 capital buffer thresholds; under disorderly transition scenarios, near-term resilience is acceptable but medium-term capital consumption from stranded asset impairments is material, and additional capital buffers may be required post-2030 under the most adverse disorderly assumptions.
claims.support_notes: Qualitative resilience conclusions and capital linkage; lacks quantified loss/capital figures.

claims.claim_text: Operational emissions for 2024 are: Scope 1 emissions 2,634.908317 tCO2e; Scope 2 emissions 6,963.4977 tCO2e (location-based) and 3,060.5382 tCO2e (market-based); Scope 3 business travel emissions 289.8833 tCO2e.
claims.support_notes: Explicit emissions metrics with units and year.

claims.claim_text: The Scope 1 boundary includes the corporate fleet (fleet emissions are included).
claims.support_notes: Boundary clarification supports faithful representation.

claims.claim_text: Target TGT001 is an absolute reduction target for Scope 1 and Scope 2 with a baseline year of 2020; progress in 2024 is 40.0% (absolute tCO2e), 25.0% (tCO2e per EUR million) and 13.3% (percentage reduction versus baseline).
claims.support_notes: Target identifier, baseline year and multiple progress measures disclosed.

claims.claim_text: For NGFS v4 Below 2°C (orderly), the scenario is aligned to a 1.8°C median temperature pathway with a carbon price trajectory from the REMIND-MAgPIE model; financial impact is assessed through loan-level probability of default sensitivity to carbon cost pass-through segmented by sector carbon intensity tier.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.4.1 Scenario analysis methods and assumptions
claims.support_notes: Methodological transparency on assumptions and impact channel.

claims.claim_text: Scope 2 emissions are disclosed on both a location-based and a market-based basis; the market-based figure reflects contractual instruments for electricity supply (e.g., renewable energy certificates and power purchase agreements) and associated emission factors.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.4.3 Emissions measurement and market-based Scope 2
claims.support_notes: Explains basis for market-based Scope 2 calculation.

claims.claim_text: Financed emissions data-quality distribution is 0.7% audited report, 35.5% CDP disclosure, 47.5% estimated using economic data and 16.3% proxy model; where proxy modelling is used, estimates are prepared on a proxy basis.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.4.4 Data-quality characteristics and proxy basis
claims.support_notes: Provides composition of input quality and notes proxy basis.

claims.claim_text: The disclosures provide multi-year information for selected measures (including climate capex and Tier 1 capital) across 2022–2024 and include change monitoring via a "changed since prior period" indicator and defined monitoring frequencies (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual).
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: 1.5 Comparative consistency and change monitoring
claims.support_notes: Explicitly describes comparability features and monitoring structure.
